playbook:
When I can afford a settlement (1 of each resource), I build the settlement rather than a road — settlements give more points for the same number of resources.

When I have exactly one brick and I will not immediately build a settlement or road this round, I do not trade away that brick unless I receive brick back or will gain a build opportunity this round — don’t trade away my only brick.

When I lack brick and a counterparty has brick, I offer 1 wood for 1 brick (or 1 grain for 1 brick) to acquire brick quickly; prioritize trading expendable resources (extra wood/grain) for brick.

When multiple resources can be traded, I prefer to give wood before grain before ore (wood > grain > ore in expendability), unless a specific build or upgrade needs ore.

When I am offered a favorable 1:1 trade that gives me brick and does not leave me unable to build next turn, I accept it.

When no counterparty has the resource I need (brick), I post no offer rather than overpay or fragment my holdings.

When I can build only a road or nothing, I consider the game state (points and remaining rounds); default to building a road only if it enables a near-term settlement or blocks an opponent — otherwise build none.

When an offer would leave me unable to reach a clear build goal in the next one or two rounds, I decline it.

Do not assume trading away resources to help opponents is worth it unless the trade directly enables a build for me that increases my score advantage.

1.text:
When I'm dealt starting resources, if I can build a settlement immediately, build it unless doing so leaves me with zero brick and I expect brick will be scarce next rounds; otherwise prefer the settlement for immediate points.

When I can afford a settlement, choose it over a road unless I specifically need a single point to tie/win.

When I'm missing one resource for a desired build, post a 1-for-1 offer to the player who has that resource, offering a resource they need (prioritize giving wood before ore).

When another player posts an offer giving me brick for my ore, accept it if I can spare the ore and it enables me to build next turn—brick is high priority.

When no one currently has brick, post offers to trade ore for brick rather than grain or wood, because securing brick unlocks both roads and settlements.

When I lack brick and no one has it, avoid spending my ore on low-value trades that don't get me brick; preserve trading currency (ore) for the critical brick trade.

When I have spare wood and someone else has grain I need for a build, offer 1 wood for 1 grain—wood is easiest to spare early.

If I cannot build this turn and no useful trades are possible, do not force offers; conserve resources and wait for better trading opportunities.

Do not trade away all my ore if doing so prevents accepting good future offers or building an ore-reliant strategy.

If an offer will let me score immediately (settlement/road), prioritize accepting or making that trade even if it costs a resource I might otherwise prefer to keep.

2.text:
When I'm able to build a settlement immediately and it yields more points than a road, I build the settlement.

When I have enough ore (>=3) and grain (>=2) to build a city next turn, I do not post offers that would trade away ore or grain needed for that city.

When another player clearly has the brick I need to build a settlement this round, I offer 1 grain for 1 brick to them.

When I lack brick and no one obvious has it, I post no offer rather than trade away grain or ore I may need for higher-value builds.

When an incoming offer would give me a resource I need but would require giving away grain needed for a city or settlement plan, I refuse it.

When an incoming offer gives me brick in exchange for a resource I can spare (not grain if I need it for a city), I accept.

When I have only enough wood+brick for a road but can instead spend my full resource set to make a settlement that scores more now, I choose the settlement.

When I'm low on wood and brick and can't build, I avoid trading away ore I might later want for a city; prioritize keeping ore unless a trade clearly enables an immediate higher-point build.

Do not make token offers just to be active; only post an offer when it directly advances a concrete build plan.
